plan.title: bug(hooks,harness): dest-lock consult-deny after first allow ghosts a retry

narratives.Description: bug(hooks,harness): dest-lock consult-deny after first allow ghosts a retry
narratives.Overview:
## Recut of the filed body

Body alignment to the bound arc. Not a new target. Do not restamp `design-critique:mechanism-shaped`.

Bound by successor lean 5587555346, verified-claims table 5587861177, and synthesis 5587864554 (dispatch SHA `eaf204355fd7d6813651ad5d25c2c219129df6a1`). That arc accepted all four classified headings. `## Repairs` maps each heading to a row. The original five-point list is withdrawn.

## Problem, restated against the tree

Grok `spawn_subagent` into a dest-proven linked worktree can allow and persist a dest-lock on the first `tool.before`, then consult-deny the same dest on a later `tool.before` (`already reserved for dispatch <incarnation>`). The child from the first allow never starts. The dest-lock stays until someone deletes it by incarnation.

This is not a same-incarnation persist miss. Dispatcher order at `eaf204355` is consult, then mint, then persist. Consult denies `reservation-conflict` on any `provenance: dispatch` lease for that dest and does not compare a presented incarnation. `mintImplementSpawnReservation` always `randomUUID()`. Grok is outside `UPDATED_INPUT_WIRE_HOSTS` (`codex`, `claude`, `cursor`), so the first incarnation cannot ride back on a second payload. A second Grok `tool.before` never reaches persist with the first identity.

Persist is the last spawn step before `allow`. The field deny text matches the consult line, not the persist-EXISTS dispatcher line. Occupied persist already `releaseSpawnReservation` for this incarnation. EXISTS catch did not write this incarnation; rolling it back would delete the winner.

Two different agents on one dest must still conflict. A retry of the same parent spawn must not consult-deny the dest the first allow already reserved when there is no live occupant. A dest-lock with no live child is leftover of an allow the host did not launch. Name that leftover-release. Do not claim persist-EXISTS denied the first launch.

## Field instance (2026-09-08, Grok Build, Windows, deftai/directive)

Through-merge resume for PRs 4249-4252. Parent `spawn_subagent` with cwd only (no `worktree_path`, no `isolation=worktree`).

Deny text (one dest shown; four dests same shape):

Directive denied spawn: destination .../4230-one-suite-step5 is already reserved for dispatch 04691d67-1470-4337-9fc5-a1bf58f961eb (agent spawn-04691d67).

Incarnations minted then denied: 04691d67, 5861cbc5, f7c51958, 865c2fae. No child process. Ghost locks under `.deft/spawn-reservations/` plus `spawn-*.json` occupancy records owned by the parent session.

Field shape: first `tool.before` persist succeeded per dest, then a later consult denied. Two process invocations of the same Grok spawn matcher, not persist-EXISTS inside one `decideHook`. Nested hook timeout is 5s in inventory; it is not proven as the missing-child cause.

Forced CLI last-resort. `cmd start` from parent `run_terminal_command` died in ~10s (Job Object). WT `Start-Process` detach survived. That recovery is #4225 / #4219, not this bug.

Investigation ledger: `.tmp/investigations/cli-worker-early-exit-2026-09-08` (`task verify:investigation` passed). Field note on #4225 comment 5586207620.

## What to build

1. Unique dest still conflicts across distinct incarnations and across parents. Keep the two-parent dest-lock test. Do not skip dest-lock for implement `general-purpose`.

2. A later `tool.before` that is a retry of the same parent spawn must not consult-deny the dest the first allow already reserved when `liveOccupant` is null. Reuse the existing dest-lock incarnation. Do not mint a new UUID. Do not treat dest+parent as a share token while a live occupant exists.

3. A dest-lock with no live occupant and no live child is leftover of an allow the host did not launch. Name an explicit leftover-release (incarnation-scoped, same as today's release). A retry after leftover-release may persist a new incarnation. Do not claim persist-EXISTS denied the first launch.

4. Keep occupied-path rollback. Do not add EXISTS rollback (that deletes the winner).

5. If a retry key is added, it must be narrower than dest+parent: dest-lock incarnation reuse without minting, or a host-stable tool identity. No `tool_call_id` exists in this tree. Env-sourced `parentId` is not an untrusted allow token for sharing a dest.

6. Logging of persist incarnation vs EXISTS is optional and does not change disposition.

7. Tests: consult-deny after first allow on one dest with no live occupant becomes reuse or leftover-release, not `already reserved`; two incarnations / two parents still conflict; occupied rollback unchanged; EXISTS conflict does not delete the winner; implement spawn still requires a unique linked worktree (#4066).

8. CHANGELOG.

## Rejected

- Same-incarnation second persist is idempotent allow (unreachable on Grok; consult denies first)
- EXISTS rollback after failed persist (no lock from this mint; would steal the winner)
- dest+parent consult-allow as the retry key (two sequential implement workers from one parent would share a dest)
- Classify grok `--cwd` as spawn-class (#4219)
- Visible TUI / WT detach recipe (#4225)
- Critic `subagent_type` plan dest skip (#4241 / PR 4251)
- Skipping dest-lock entirely for implement `general-purpose`
- Documenting CLI as the real Grok Build launch path

## Acceptance

- [ ] Two `tool.before` invocations for one Grok `spawn_subagent` on one dest-proven cwd, first allow persisted, no live occupant: the second consult does not deny `already reserved` and does not leave a ghost dest-lock a human must delete by incarnation
- [ ] Two different dispatch incarnations on the same dest still conflict
- [ ] Two parents on the same dest still conflict
- [ ] Occupied persist still releases this incarnation; EXISTS conflict does not delete the winner
- [ ] `general-purpose` implement spawn still requires a unique linked worktree (#4066)
- [ ] CHANGELOG

## Non-goals

- Do not fold into #4219, #4225, or #4241
- Do not dest-root-swap ritual/scope
- Do not punch capability-mode / read-only as a spawn unlock
- Do not make `--always-approve` the documented default
- Do not restamp this issue for a second arc
- Do not implement #4258 here (Recut-lean ingest harvest). This body recut is so current harvest can read these AC checkboxes.

## Repairs (accepted headings -> this body)

| Heading | Class | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same-incarnation persist is unreachable on the Grok field path | blocks-the-design | Problem restated; rejected first bullet; What to build 2 (reuse, no new mint) |
| Persist success means the first hook allowed; dest-lock is not proven to be why the first child never started | blocks-the-design | Problem restated; field shape; What to build 3 (leftover-release); AC 1 |
| Remedy 2 (rollback failed persist) does not clear the field ghost and can steal a winner | sharpens-framing | What to build 4; AC occupied/EXISTS |
| Dest+parent without a presented incarnation is not a safe substitute for unique dest | sharpens-framing | What to build 1, 2, 5; rejected dest+parent bullet |

## Related

- #4215 (closed) -- dest-proven skip of parent ritual; Grok dest is cwd only
- #4066 -- dest-lock create / incarnation-scoped release
- #4219 -- CLI argv spawn-class (recovery path, not this deny)
- #4225 -- visible TUI / last-resort detach
- #1185 -- implement spawn mutation gates
- #4258 -- Recut lean still harvests issue-body AC; this recut is the body-alignment workaround, not that mapper

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-08T15:21:54Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

charter: refutation
round: 1
ceiling: 5587371827
sha: eaf204355fd7d6813651ad5d25c2c219129df6a1

Refutation target (as dispatched): a second PreToolUse persist/consult for one spawn_subagent on the same dest-proven cwd is a foreign reservation (already reserved) rather than an idempotent same-incarnation allow, and that ghost dest-lock is why the child never starts.

Verdict: the first clause is true as a dest-keyed conflict, and false as a same-incarnation miss. The second clause does not follow from the persist success the field already recorded. The five-point remedy cannot bind as written.

SHA-pinned reads used origin/master eaf204355fd7d6813651ad5d25c2c219129df6a1 (GitHub raw of that commit). Local HEAD 7236655ef6f586169c94f3c4ce5eeccf5668960b is not the target.

### 1. Same-incarnation persist is unreachable on the Grok field path

blocks-the-design

Evidence (measured at eaf204355):

- consultImplementSpawnOccupancy denies reservation-conflict when existingDispatchReservation finds any provenance: dispatch lease on that dest. The deny names the existing incarnation and agent id. It does not compare presented incarnation, parentId, or tool identity (packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts 235-248, 413-423).
- Dispatcher order is consult first, then later gates, then mintImplementSpawnReservation then persistSpawnReservation (packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts 1343-1366 and 1694-1724). A second decideHook never reaches persist once consult denies.
- mintImplementSpawnReservation always does randomUUID() (452-458). It does not read the dest-lock.
- Grok is outside UPDATED_INPUT_WIRE_HOSTS (codex, claude, cursor only; dispatcher.ts 2065-2068). spawnUpdatedInput returns undefined on Grok (1775). The first incarnation cannot ride back on a second PreToolUse payload.
- persistSpawnReservation uses containedWrite mode create and maps CONTAINED_WRITE_EXISTS to { ok: false, reason: "conflict" } with no same-incarnation read (562-575). A second persist of even the same reservation object conflicts.
- Field deny text on the issue ("already reserved for dispatch 04691d67-… (agent spawn-04691d67)") matches the consult message, not the persist-EXISTS message ("is already reserved. Own worktree means a unique reservation." dispatcher.ts 1719-1723).
- No tool_call_id / toolCallId / call_id symbol exists in this tree.

Failure mode: shipping remedy 1 (same-incarnation second persist is idempotent allow) leaves the field deny intact. The second Grok tool.before is a new mint identity with an empty presented incarnation. Consult treats it as a foreign reservation because that is the dest-keyed rule, not because persist forgot to be idempotent.

Disposition: do not bind remedy 1 as the AC. Name an idempotency key that a second Grok PreToolUse actually presents (dest-lock contents plus parentId is one candidate; a host tool-call id is not in inventory). Keep two-distinct-incarnation conflict.

### 2. Persist success means the first hook allowed; dest-lock is not proven to be why the first child never started

blocks-the-design

Evidence:

- Persist is the last spawn step before verdict allow / spawn-ready (dispatcher.ts 1711-1741). Field note and #4225 comment 5586207620 say first PreToolUse persist succeeded for four incarnations, then second consult denied. That is first-allow leftover plus retry-deny, not persist-then-deny inside one decideHook.
- Grok deposit has one spawn matcher (Task|SubagentStart|spawn_subagent|start_agent|CreateAgent) and no failClosed (.grok/hooks/deft.json 25-33; nested timeout 5s, NESTED_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS in packages/core/src/init-deposit/agent-hooks.ts 55-56). This is not the Cursor ApplyPatch double-matcher class (#2764). Two PreToolUse on one dest are two process invocations of the same matcher.
- The locked test "keeps persist/reservation-conflict as the final launch refusal after two dest-proven consults" uses parent-1 then parent-2 (packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts 215-244). It encodes two-parent unique dest, not one spawn_subagent double-fired.
- Consult-without-persist is already two-allow (spawn-occupancy.test.ts 580-616). The conflict appears only after the first persist.

Failure mode: treating the dest-lock as the launch suppressor explains why a retry cannot start. It does not explain why the host did not create a child after the first allow. Collapse of those two events into one AC (do not deny already reserved and do not leave a ghost) can ship an idempotent second allow while the first allow still produces no pid (timeout after persist, empty nested allow, or a second user-level spawn_subagent call).

Disposition: split the AC. (a) Unique dest still conflicts across incarnations/parents. (b) A second tool.before that is a retry of the same parent spawn must not consult-deny the dest the first allow already reserved. (c) A dest-lock without a live child is a leftover of an allow the host did not launch; that leftover needs an explicit release rule, not the claim that persist-EXISTS denied the first launch. Do not bind until the host last-verdict / timeout-after-persist / two-call shape is named.

### 3. Remedy 2 (rollback failed persist) does not clear the field ghost and can steal a winner

sharpens-framing

Evidence:

- On EXISTS, persist did not write this incarnation (catch and return conflict; spawn-occupancy.ts 571-573). There is no that dest-lock from this mint to roll back.
- On occupied after a successful create, persist already releaseSpawnReservation for this incarnation (577-579).
- Dispatcher after !persisted.ok denies and does not release (1712-1724). Release on EXISTS would delete the other incarnation that won create.
- Field ghost is a successful persist plus occupancy spawn-*.json owned by the parent, then a later consult deny. Remedy 2 never runs on that path.

Failure mode: a test "failed persist does not leave a lock" is already true for occupied and would be a unique-reservation hole if it deleted EXISTS winners. The ghost the operator had to delete by incarnation is the first success.

Disposition: keep occupied rollback. Do not add EXISTS rollback. If the lean wants failed spawn does not poison the dest, say which failure: consult deny after a prior allow, host timeout after persist, or persist occupied. Those are different releases.

### 4. Dest+parent without a presented incarnation is not a safe substitute for unique dest

sharpens-framing

Evidence:

- existingDispatchReservation is dest-only (235-248). Two parents on one dest already conflict by design (spawn-occupancy.test.ts 223-252; dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts 215-244).
- parentId is DEFT_SESSION_ID / DEFT_SESSION_NAME / GROK_SESSION_ID / none (142-149). Grok reservation identitySourceKind is host-env (467). That is session occupancy, not a spawn tool-call.
- Two sequential spawn_subagent calls from one parent onto one dest-proven cwd are indistinguishable from a host double-fire of one call. #4066 unique reservation says those two agents must still conflict (issue AC and rejected skip dest-lock for implement general-purpose).
- allocatedWorktreeMatches already requires presented incarnation; dest-lock does not substitute a missing one (644-656).

Failure mode: consult-allow when existing.parentId equals this parentId would let one orchestrator launch two implement workers onto one linked worktree. Swarm dest-lock under reservationLockRoot (main clone) is shared state; that hole is cross-worktree.

Disposition: if retry-allow is the fix, the key must be narrower than dest+parent: dest-lock incarnation reuse without minting, or a host-stable tool identity. Do not drop the two-parent test. Injection lens: env-sourced parentId is not an untrusted-input allow token for sharing a dest.

### 5. Inventory already covers unique dest; the missing piece is retry identity, not a new lock type

footnote

Existing mechanisms: dest-lock create, incarnation-scoped release, consult-before-mint, dest-proven parent-ritual skip (#4215), Grok cwd-only dest, liveOccupant deny, two-parent dest-lock. Missing: persist same-incarnation allow; consult reuse of an existing reservation; hook log of persist incarnation vs EXISTS; Grok updatedInput. Logging (issue point 4) does not change disposition.

### Injection / swarm lens

The target is shared dest-lock state under the main clone, used at implement-spawn concurrency. Unique dest across parents and incarnations must stay fail-closed. Retry-allow that keys only on parent session id is a cohort hole. Grok cannot rewrite spawn input, so incarnation transport used by Claude/Cursor/Codex is not available as the retry proof.

### Road not taken

Chose: refute same-incarnation persist miss caused never-start and require a presented retry key plus a split AC.

Rejected: bind the five-point list and treat consult-deny after persist as the same bug as persist-EXISTS.

Steelmans of the rejected position: #4066 unique dest is working; the child never started because the host ignored the first allow (5s nested timeout after persist, or empty nested allow). Flip if a field run shows two deft-hook --host grok --event tool.before processes for one spawn_subagent, first stdout spawn-ready, no child pid, second stdout the consult already-reserved line, and the host treats the second as the spawn verdict. That would make clause two true as last-verdict, still without making remedy 1 reachable on Grok without a consult change.

The dest-keyed foreign-reservation half of the target stands. The same-incarnation-allow half and the never-start causal half do not. Recut the remedy around consult reuse or an explicit leftover-release, and keep two-incarnation conflict.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-08T15:22:26Z)

## In plain English

The persist-then-deny story on #4254 does not bind as written. The field deny is dest-keyed consult after a first allow already persisted, not a same-incarnation persist miss, and the dest-lock does not prove why the first child never started. Confirming this map recuts the next-build contract around consult reuse or leftover-release, keeps two-incarnation conflict, and does not land code. Ingest stays a later operator verb after a completed-arc record.

Total over the denominator, every take accept-into-contract, empty disagreement set, zero unresolved audit markers, the one same-round sibling posted. Operator has not confirmed this map yet.

## Bound remedy (reading of the takes)

1. Do not bind issue remedy 1 (same-incarnation second persist is idempotent allow) as the AC. A second Grok tool.before consult-denies before mint/persist; mint always randomUUID; Grok has no updatedInput wire.
2. Split the AC. Unique dest still conflicts across incarnations and parents. A retry of the same parent spawn must not consult-deny the dest the first allow already reserved. A dest-lock without a live child is leftover of an allow the host did not launch; name an explicit release rule. Do not claim persist-EXISTS denied the first launch.
3. Keep occupied rollback. Do not add EXISTS rollback (that would delete the winner).
4. If retry-allow is the fix, the key must be narrower than dest+parent. Do not drop the two-parent unique-dest test. Env-sourced parentId is not an allow token for sharing a dest.
5. Logging of persist incarnation vs EXISTS does not change disposition.

This map is an offer. Confirm or amend before bind.
